# Multi-sample Single-cell RNA-seq in Bioconductor

Multi-sample scRNA-seq analysis broadly follows the same analysis steps as for single-sample, but there are some key differences.
The process is well described in [OSCA](https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.multisample/).

Below, a demo multi-sample dataset is suggested, containing single-cell data from 8 matched lupus patients before and after IFN stimulation, which can be used for self-directed learning.

## Learning goal

Using [OSCA](https://bioconductor.org/books/release/OSCA.multisample/) multi-sample chapter as a reference, adapt and extend the single-sample workflow to data with multiple donors and conditions.

## Learning objectives

By working through this notebook you should be able to:

1. Describe the structure of a multi-sample, multi-condition experiment (donors, conditions and how they are paired).
2. Adapt QC and clustering to multiple samples, and check for donor or batch effects.
3. Explain why donors, not individual cells, are the unit of replication when comparing conditions, and outline a pseudobulk differential expression approach.

## Data loading

Data used are from Kang HM, et al. (2018). Multiplexed droplet single-cell RNA-sequencing using
natural genetic variation. *Nature Biotechnology* 36:89–94. [doi:10.1038/nbt.4042](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042).
PBMCs from 8 lupus patients, control and IFN-β stimulated, distributed via the muscData Bioconductor package.
